questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The location had a big impact, but also dorms and the curriculum was a huge part of choosing.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The school had great teachers and it seemed like a very prestine school. It had a lot of tests too, but most of them made sense to have and let you see how well you had learned the previous chapters.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fairly easy, the school was very good at sending out information.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We could get on a bus from the airport to our dorms on the day of arrival.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: The dorm I lived in was a part of Nanzan university, it was just not located on campus but a 20 minute walk from it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is nice to have "your own" place, but I can also imagine that some people might feel like they miss out on things by not living close to most of the other students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For the japanese language courses there is a multiplechoice test and then from that they place you on a level. For the other courses you just choose what you want, mark it on a paper, hand it in and they accept it. Afterwards you have some time to try the chosen courses and change if you want to.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Descriptions of the courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succesful.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take your time to choose and don't worry about being lock in the course since it is possible to change (within a specific time).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Courses are marked as "A" like "Religion A", but you can't take it lower than that, and it wasn't that hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More tests and all the Japanese courses are of course in Japanese. Everything counted towards the final grade, so all from homework, test to attendance.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Intensive Japanese 2, Japanese Religion A and Japanese Culture and Art A

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Japanese culture and art A was really good! The teacher is super chill and we look at art and historical buldings and other things from Japan. It was a really nice course and really chill.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Had to get a national insurence, even though I was covered with my insurance from Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food (unless you buy a lot of veggies and fruit) and clothing is a lot less expensive, transportation too.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know.. I was not a part of it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and explore the city. Go to cities close by. Experience Japan.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took some time, but it wasn't too hard.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that they bike on the sidewalks. You had to keep an eye out all the time to make sure there wasn't a bike coming your way.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The respect and orderlyness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Go to class - study - but also enjoy the time you have.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Keeping up with the Japanese class. With all the tests it was hard to do some "extra" studying.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
